c1421.summary: Syama Sastri pleads with Kamakshi of Kanchipuram: this is the time to protect me — don't say 'tomorrow'.
m: Devi, this is the time to protect me.
Come very quickly and end my sorrows —
have compassion, Shankari, Kamakshi.
Mother of the world, have you no mercy on me?
Am I not your servant, O dweller in Kanchi, Kalyani?
For you, the beloved of Ekamreshvara,
why, Mother, is this such a burden? Listen, Mother.
Sister of Shyama Krishna, Kaumari, with lips red as bimba fruit, Gauri,
golden-limbed, Lalita, supreme goddess,
Kamakshi, apart from you, on this earth, with love
who is there to protect me, Mother?
If you say 'tomorrow, the day after', I won't listen; I cannot bear it any more;
show compassion this very day; look on me with grace.
Ever holding your lotus feet in my mind,
I have longed for your protection, Mother — (protect) me with joy.

c8801.summary: What other refuge is there? Syama Sastri trusts Minakshi of Madurai alone.
m: What other refuge is there on earth, Mother, to protect me?
I have always trusted, trusted, that you alone protect those who surrender, Minakshi.
Dwelling in Madurai, whose lotus feet are served by Sarasvati and Lakshmi,
destroyer of Madhu and Kaitabha, Katyayani, of swan-like gait, dwelling at the end of the Vedas,
grant me a boon and protect me quickly, Shiva's consort, Mother — is this a burden to you?
Are you not the great giver, Shankari? Even Brahma and the others are protected by you.
Holding a parrot, dark one, sister of cloud-dark Krishna, Kaumari,
bearing the spotless crescent, with bimba-red lips, boundless treasure of grace — protect me.
Holding your two feet in my heart I have prayed; listen, you of stately elephant gait.
Even when others praise you, you grant boons; always, never forgetting you in my mind,
O wife of Manmatha's enemy, if I praise you, holding you in my heart as my refuge,
to joyfully grant the fruit — on earth, you alone delight in protecting those who bow.

c1111.summary: Syama Sastri tells Minakshi he has always trusted her lotus feet, and asks why she delays.
m: Lotus-petal-eyed daughter of the snow mountain, your
lotus feet
I have always trusted, Mother; grant me good, Sri Minakshamma.
Without delay, giver of boons — is there another god in the world like you?
Is there?
Ancient one, holding a parrot, with a braid dark as bees, Sadashiva's
queen.
Is it not your very title that you fulfil the wishes of all who come to you?
Is this a burden?
Protect me, Mother, abode of compassion; I cannot bear it any longer.
O moon-faced one, how much I have pleaded with you to show compassion;
why such delay, Mother? It is not proper — you are compassionate.
Delighting in Sama music, abode of virtues, praised by Shyama Krishna (Mother),
(giver of) happiness,
dark Goddess, you alone are my refuge, granter of all desires —
protect me.

c2442.summary: Protect me, Kamakshi; Syama Sastri marvels at her radiant form and feels his life fulfilled by seeing her feet.
m: Protect me, Kamakshi, holy one, destroyer of sin.
Though I have always pleaded with you in many ways, why do you act like this? Remove my sorrow quickly.
(svara-sahitya passage)
O Lalita, dwelling on the golden mountain, I who constantly worship you am your own; hear me, O you hailed by all the worlds; now end our sins and grant boons.
To good people who think of you in their hearts, at all times, joy
you grant; that you fulfil the heart's desires — you have earned that lovely name.
Embodiment of compassion, Mother who protected the world — am I not your child? Cherish me.
Such a form, so radiant, such fame and splendour, embodiment of virtues —
even searching the three worlds, is there another? What penance did I do in a past life, that your
lotus feet I have seen again and again and am fulfilled? Listen to my plea.
Your presence shines with the jewels at the edge of the crowns of kings of kings,
Goddess, giver of boons to all people, moon-faced, praised by Shyama Krishna,
queen of Kanchipura, with eyes like blooming lotus petals, witness of the world, gracious Parashakti.

c1293.summary: A Sanskrit prayer to Kamakshi, who roams on the golden mountain, the ferry across worldly life.
m: Mother who roams on the golden mountain, young Kamakoti, of noble character,
praised by Brahma and Hari, Goddess, daughter of the snow mountain, Lalita — always
protect me who bows to you, consort of Shankara, chaste one, great Tripurasundari,
Shyamalambika, ferry across the ocean of worldly life, protector of Shyama Krishna, Mother,
giver of the fruits one desires, Kamakshi, witness of all worlds.

c1009.summary: A Sanskrit prayer to Kamakshi, daughter of the snow mountain, dwelling at the centre of Meru.
m: Daughter of the snow mountain, protect me,
giver of boons, supreme goddess,
dwelling at the centre of Sumeru (Mother),
Sri Kamakshi.
Golden-limbed, lotus-eyed,
daughter of Matanga,
praised by Brahma, Hari and Shiva,
the gods and great sages,
with a face like the moon,
with a neck shining with
a necklace of pearls and gems,
wish-fulfilling creeper of devotees,
sister of Shyama Krishna, Gauri,
Supreme Goddess, daughter of the
mountain, with a dark braid, with
a parrot's sweet speech, Sri Lalita.

c8817.summary: O Mother of the world, protect me quickly; Syama Sastri asks Kamakshi to forgive his faults.
m: O Mother of the world, protect me quickly, Mother.
In this world, who else is people's refuge? Radiant one, praised by kings,
moon-faced, lotus-eyed, shining with virtues, Kamakshi.
My own mother — is it fitting to ignore me, so close to you? Am I not one who trusts you?
Is protecting one like me so rare? You protect all the worlds, gracious one,
Annapurna, giver of boons, hear my plea and grant your presence, remover of the fear of the distressed;
why delay, daughter of the mountain? I cannot bear it, Mother; apart from you, for protection,
did I fickly trust other gods? Wherever I am, my nature (is devoted to you), O lover of music,
delight of the heart, queen of the blue-throated one — I trusted you; truly, have mercy;
I am fickle-minded; what past deeds have I brought with me? O Kamakshi of Kanchi, I
have praised you; refuge, refuge — grant it; fickle as I am, keep me in your care, Mother.
Praised by Shyama Krishna, Goddess who grants good fame, forgive and bear my faults,
beloved of the lord of the noble white mountain, Parashakti, listen to my plea.
(Is it fair) to grant boons to wicked rulers who know no propriety when they praise you?

c3299.summary: Parvati, I have trusted you completely — why delay in protecting me?
m: Parvati, I have trusted you completely; why delay in protecting me, you with a parrot in hand, of noble character?
Whose lotus feet are worshipped by the gods, lover of music, abode of virtues — why delay, Kamakshi?
Sister of Shyama Krishna, Shivashankari, Gauri, abode of virtues, dweller in Kamapitha, Shambhavi, Mrdani.

c8810.summary: Protect me quickly, Lalita: I have wasted my time praising wicked men for money.
m: Protect me quickly, Lalita; I am one who has trusted you completely, creeper that fulfils devotees' wishes.
Apart from you, who is our refuge, Mother? Our Mother — very quickly
come without delay and show compassion; won't you hear my cry?
Parashakti, whose feet the gods worship, I am your devotee, always.
Whose story is praised by Brahma, Vishnu, Shankara and Indra,
ancient one, worshipped by Vani and Indrani, queen of the one adorned with serpents,
praising again and again the stories of arrogant, wicked people,
I always wandered after them for money; remove all my sorrows and grant a boon,
dwelling at the centre of Sumeru, sister of Shyama Krishna, Kaumari,
Uma, Mother Minakshi, Shankari, O great queen — this is the time to protect me.

c8834.summary: A prayer to Akhilandeshvari of Tiruvanaikaval (Jambukeshvaram) to grant good.
m: Shankari, grant good, moon-faced Akhilandeshvari, Shambhavi, worshipped by Brahma, Gauri, Mother,
remover of distress, destroyer of foes, Kalyani, ever granting fruits to those who bow, Hara's consort, Mother of the world,
delighting with the lord of Jambu, joyful in protecting the world, conch-necked Bhavani, bearer of the skull, wielder of the trident,
delighting Manmatha's enemy, nourisher of all worlds, giver of auspiciousness, Mridani, of swan-like gait,
sister of Shyama Krishna, dark one, slender-waisted, delighting in Sama music, young one, ever inclined to destroy sorrow.

c1051.summary: Syama Sastri asks Tripurasundari for health and a sound body. (The karnatik.com text of this song is irregular; meanings of some lines are approximate.)
m: Quickly, looking on me with grace, always
(grant me) health, a sturdy body — grant me,
grant me, grant me, grant me.
Most holy one, compassionate one, I praise you;
most holy one, compassionate one, I praise you,
whose lotus feet (I worship), queen of the remover of the sorrows of those who bow,
why this indifference? (I trust) your great
lotus-like virtues, Tripurasundari.
(Chittaswaram, sung to the same svaras:)
Lotus-eyed one, protector of those who bow,
the Vedas cry out to you —
lotus-eyed one, protector of those who bow,
the Vedas cry out to you —
who is your equal? Hear my plea and show compassion;
now let the indifference end.
With lovely tresses dark as clouds,
praised in rich, fine poetry,
with a gracious smile,
(sung vowels)
with a face lovely as the lotus,
praised by Brahma, the lord of speech,
Narayani — listen to Shyama Krishna,
hear my plea, daughter of the mountain.

c8772.summary: Grant boons quickly and protect me, Kamakshi; why turn away?
m: Grant boons quickly and protect me; I have trusted you completely,
enchantress of Shiva, Sri Kamakshi.
Without delay — are you not the treasury of compassion? Why turn away now? Listen, lotus-faced one.
Granter of desired fruits, Goddess, wish-creeper to those who bow, ancient one, of sweet speech, queen of Shiva,
sister of Shyama Krishna, Gauri, Supreme Goddess, Girija — won't you come to protect the helpless?

c1108.summary: Swati Tirunal's hymn to Padmanabha of Thiruvananthapuram, describing his form, his legend with the sage Divakara, and the temple's festivals.
m: I meditate on the one reclining on the king of serpents, the giver of the four aims of life,
the eternal Person,
whose feet are worshipped by Brahma, Shiva, Indra and the gods
and the celestials — Padmanabha;
dwelling in a wondrous jewelled palace on an island in the milk ocean,
ever worshipped by Narada and all the sages, the divine attendants and the king of birds,
served by shining weapons such as the radiant Sudarshana and Nandaka,
intent on supporting those who bow at his feet, caressed by Lakshmi's lotus hands — Padmanabha;
who came to earth through the merit of the great devotee, the ascetic Divakara,
whose head was fondled with delight on beholding his lovely, wondrous child form,
who was prevented by the yogi's hand from snatching the salagrama meant for worship,
who settled at the feet of the ascetic who followed swiftly, intent on compassion and joy — Padmanabha;
pleased by the worship of the ascetics who praise him,
whose Padma tirtha and other waters, clear as lotuses, removing impurity,
destroy all sins,
praised by Agastya, Mahendra, Trikuta and the best of
the Malaya mountains,
(honoured by) Martanda Varma of Vanchi, shining in the golden
vimana —
Padmanabha;
adorned with a crown of ruby-red gems, makara earrings, necklaces and the Kaustubha,
wrapped in yellow silk, adorned with a girdle and a fine forest garland,
delighting in the daily festivals such as the lakshadipam offered by the faultless king of Vanchi,
his eyes, long as the petals of the lotus from his navel, brimming with the nectar of compassion —
Padmanabha.

c1176.summary: O God of gods, I contemplate the service of your lotus feet — Swati Tirunal's prayer to Padmanabha.
m: O God of gods, I contemplate the service of your lotus feet.
Lord of the three worlds, with abundant compassion, my
worldly anguish, all of it, remove, beloved of Lakshmi.
Sung by the hosts of great ascetics, whose holy story destroys terrible sins, for those devoted to hearing it daily,
eager to fulfil the desires of such people, with a most charming glance,
most skilled in removing the elephant's unbearable foe, whose blessed feet are worshipped by Indra and the gods,
grant good; praised by Brahma, born of your lotus navel, and Sarasvati,
supremely pleased Lord,
clad in garments like gold, worshipped since birth — remove here all the heap of my sins, with compassion,
destroyer of the hosts of demons, friend of the humble, protect me, wish-tree to the wise who seek refuge, Sri
Padmanabha, Shauri.

c6804.summary: Protect me with compassion, Shauri (Padmanabha), ship across the ocean of worldly life.
m: Protect me with compassion, Shauri, abode of the essence of mercy, ender of sin and suffering,
clad in gold, with a fair moon-like face, Sri Padmanabha, lotus-eyed,
whose lotus feet shine with the lovely golden crowns of the gods, skilled in crushing great pride,
eager for pure devotion, ever ready to grant every desire to all who serve alike, with a most lovely glance,
with a gentle smile shining like jasmine, delighting the hosts of gods intent on praise,
wish-tree to those who bow, of a form as beautiful as Manmatha's,
grant me well-being joyfully, with teeth like rubies, the fine ship across the matchless ocean of worldly life,
whose story is sung by Narada and hosts of sages — remove all my sins, Lord.

c2634.summary: A padam in which the heroine teases her lord: enough of your sweet words!
m: Enough, enough of all these sweet-sounding words!
Lotus-eyed one, how pleased you are — how fine!
Has the moon turned kind? It has become great fortune for that woman, O lovely one;
so this is how our fortune has turned out, handsome one!
Listen to my plea, Lord; I have trusted you; what more, O great one
who shines on Shesha, Sri Padmanabha?

c6677.summary: A Malayalam padam: a heroine tells her friend of the torment of love as evening falls and her beloved Padmanabha does not come.
m: Friend with curling hair, how can I tell you the anguish caused by the flower-arrowed (Kama)?
The sun has sunk into the ocean; the Malaya breeze — alas, my mind is utterly overwhelmed, friend.
Longing grows in my heart; my body grows weak, O sweet-voiced one;
in the flower garden, the humming of the bees — hearing it, desire grows in my mind, friend.
Even the moon has now become burning embers; the flower-arrowed one has become my enemy, O moon-faced one;
the chatter of the parrot pains me greatly — tell me quickly, lovely one,
is my beloved, beautiful as a rain cloud, lotus-eyed, lotus-navelled, angry with me?
Alas, his heart is full of compassion — why this coolness now? Fulfil my wish quickly.

c6956.summary: A Hindi song describing Shiva, lord of Srigiri, dancing in the hall to the sound of drums.
m: Shankara, lord of Srigiri, the Lord, shining in dance in the wondrous hall,
smeared with ash, three-eyed, wearing a garland of skulls; with him dance Bhringi and the ganas.
'tvanana tanana nanana' sound the drums; the gods and sages shine in assembly in the sky;
'dhrukuta dhim tadhim' resound the drums;
'ta tai takita taka' — the rhythm shines in the beat; he shines in the lotus of Padmanabha's heart.

c1019.summary: Protect me always, Mother, slayer of Mahishasura, younger sister of Padmanabha.
m: Protect me always, Mother, slayer of Mahishasura.
Lovely as the moon's orb, fair-faced, ever granting all desires to those who serve, with playful glance (Mother),
bee to the lotus face of Shiva, whose story is sung by Narada and hosts of sages,
whose lotus feet shine with the lovely jewelled crowns of Brahma and the hosts of gods,
whose body shines with radiant gold and divine ornaments, whose eyes humble the pride of lotus petals,
with a gentle, gracious smile that enchants the sages, wish-creeper to those who bow, daughter of the mountain,
grant me well-being always, younger sister of Padmanabha, ever intent on removing the sorrows of worldly life,
with a braid lovely as a fresh rain cloud, skilled in destroying the hosts of fierce demons.

c1366.summary: A Hindi song on the darshan of Vishveshvara at Kashi, where the Ganga flows like milk.
m: When I had the darshan of Vishveshvara with great love,
the treasure of compassion cut the noose of birth and death.
In his city flows the Ganga, like milk; on its banks, at every ghat, sannyasins throng.
Ash on his limbs, trident in hand, a garland of serpents shining on his chest, Girija as half his body — the three worlds are his servants.
Lotus-navelled, lotus-eyed (Vishnu), and three-eyed Shambhu Mahesha — worship these two forms and become immortal.

c1817.summary: Rama, boundary of all virtues — dwell always in my heart.
m: Rama, Rama, boundary of virtues, Rama, delight of the heart, (Lord of) Sita,
moon-faced, dark as a cloud, clad in gold, slayer of enemies,
whose feet are worshipped by Indra and the gods, dwell always in my heart, with enchanting elephant-like gait,
who broke the pride of the wicked, destroyer of the anguish of worldly life, with eyes full of compassion,
surrounded by hosts of monkeys, Lord, grant me well-being every day,
with a necklace of new gems, who humbled the ocean's pride, who crossed the ocean, of beautiful form,
friend of the humble, protect me, destroyer of the ten-headed one, wish-tree to those who bow, in the form of Padmanabha,
dwelling in the hearts of sages, with a lovely musk tilaka, with a forest garland, beloved of Vaidehi.

c6961.summary: A hymn to the goddess of Kumarakoil (Sri Kumaranagara), describing her beauty.
m: O dweller in Sri Kumaranagara, abode of compassion, abode of Lakshmi,
wish-tree to those who seek refuge, bee to the lotus face of Sri Padmanabha,
with lovely tinkling anklets, radiant with jingling bracelets on your hands,
with a lovely moon-like face, with hair adorned with fresh lotus petals,
whose kohl-dark glances are a mass of beauty,
pure-hearted one, delighting in play in the bower, protect me, with a musk tilaka,
with a neck like the noble conch, Mother of the world, protector of the earth,
with lips lovely as bimba fruit, with hair shining like swarms of bees,
Mother, whose radiance mocks clusters of white lotuses,
whose feet are worshipped by Shiva, Vishnu and Manmatha, giver of good to those who bow at your feet,
whose slow gait outdoes the elephant, who repels the enemies of the gods,
Indira, cause of the worlds, with teeth like rubies, with tender sprout-like feet,
whose gentle smile shames the moon's rays, lovely as clusters of jasmine and drops of honey,
lotus-faced, worshipped by the world.

c1367.summary: A hymn to Sarasvati, Mother of the world, holding the veena and book — sung during Navaratri.
m: Goddess, Mother of the world, Goddess, grant me with grace devotion to your feet,
whose feet shine with the jewels of the gods' crowns, full of pure bliss, with a parrot's sweet speech, Vani,
whose palms shine with the veena and book, seated on a fine white lotus, Mother,
whose lovely braid surpasses the spreading rain clouds,
with eyes like a doe's, skilled in removing (suffering), who takes away the sins of those who bow,
shining with great jewelled ornaments, protector of the wise,
consort of Brahma, pleasing the sages, supreme, beyond measure, imperishable,
abode of all arts, Sharada, with a face lovely as the moon,
enchanting with brows like Manmatha's bow and its string,
whose beautiful feet are worshipped by Shuka, Sanaka and the great sages,
wearing the moon on matted locks, seated on a pure lotus,
with feet like blooming lotuses, beyond difference, who has destroyed sorrow,
adorned with luminous new necklaces and a girdle of a hundred strands of light,
Mother, adorned by the Mimamsa and the Agamas,
shining with the virtues of the creeper of captivating sound and gamaka,
shining with the Padma and other Puranas, praised in song,
pure-hearted, possessed of knowledge, first of the three worlds, faultless,
with lips redder than coral, shining with a gentle white smile,
full of compassion, ever ready to protect those who come for refuge,
whose heart is delighted by the Navaratri festival performed by devotees, pure one,
show compassion to me who worship you, with teeth like jasmine buds,
giver of abundant good, queen who removes sin, delighting in praise.

c1279.summary: Purandaradasa marvels that Yashoda played with the uplifter of the world as her own child.
m: Yashoda played with the uplifter of the world.
Thinking him her son, Yashoda played with the uplifter of the world, the abode of virtues, Ranga.
Yashoda played with the one of countless glories whom even the Vedas cannot grasp, the ruby among children.
Yashoda played with the one subtler than the atom, greater than the great, immeasurable.
Yashoda played with the Supreme Person, Paravasudeva, Purandara Vitthala.

c4682.summary: Purandaradasa invites Lakshmi, goddess of fortune, to come with tinkling anklets into the homes of devotees.
m: Come, Lakshmi of fortune, our Mother; come, Lakshmi of good fortune.
Step by step, with your anklet bells ringing,
at the time of worship by good and saintly people, like butter rising from buttermilk,
come showering gold; reveal fulfilment to people's minds,
shining with the radiance of ten million suns, daughter of King Janaka — come quickly.
Without leaving, (stay) in the homes of devotees — daily great festivals, daily auspiciousness;
doll who shines in the minds of true and saintly people,
giving countless fortunes, come turning the bangles on your hands,
marked with kumkum, lotus-eyed, proud queen of Venkataramana,
making rivers of sugar and ghee flow, at the time of the Friday worship,
beloved of Alagiri Ranga, queen of beautiful Purandara Vitthala.

c1117.summary: Purandaradasa prays to Ganesha, son of Gauri, for the grace to always remember Vitthala.
m: Elephant-faced one, I pray to you, son of Gauri,
worshipped by the three worlds, protector of good people,
bearer of the noose and goad, supremely holy,
rider of the mouse, beloved of the sages.
Joyfully show me your feet,
O one worshipped by the good, with affection;
bless me so that I always remember Purandara Vitthala,
the lotus-navelled Lord — have mercy.

c1485.summary: A hymn to Venkateshvara of Tirumala, recalling his deeds as Krishna and Rama.
m: (I worship) the dweller on Venkatachala, the dweller in Vaikuntha,
lotus-eyed, supremely holy, holding conch and discus, of the form of pure consciousness,
praised by lotus-born Brahma, of countless virtues and names,
who delights in the music of Tumburu and Narada, who reclines on the ocean, delight of the soul,
who took the Pandavas' side, destroyer of the Kauravas' pride, whose arms'
valour is complete, who removed the fear of Ahalya's curse,
the essence of all the Vedas, (dwelling in) all living beings,
wearing makara earrings, Madana Gopala,
nurturer of devotees, Sri Purandara Vitthala.

c5409.summary: Chant the Rama mantra — it is the essence of the Vedas and the root of the path to liberation.
m: Chant the Rama mantra, O man.
Don't ruin yourself trusting this mantra and that; it is the one Shiva taught his wife.
The mantra that perfects bathing and silence; the mantra men meditate on in their minds;
the mantra that drives away base qualities; what to say — the mantra that was the essence for Vibhishana;
the mantra that is the essence of all the Vedas, the root mantra on the path to liberation,
the mantra that at once reveals the taste of devotion, the great mantra of Purandara Vitthala, treasure of bliss.
